title: Write Like It's 1866: LLMs Relearn Telegraphese
summary: An exploration of how modern LLMs adapt to historical communication constraints, specifically testing whether AI models can relearn 'telegraphese' - the ultra-concise writing style from 1866 when telegraph messages were prohibitively expensive. The experiment reveals how cost-driven communication patterns from the Victorian era can be used as a framework for understanding AI language generation behavior.
problem_solved: Tests whether LLMs can adapt to historical communication style constraints that prioritized brevity due to economic factors
why_valuable: Demonstrates a creative methodology for understanding AI language generation by imposing historical stylistic constraints, revealing insights about LLM adaptability and communication patterns
